title: The Citadel
why: The NHS opened its doors on 5 July 1948; this is the film about a doctor and the money in medicine that helped make the case for it.

title: Wimbledon
why: The first Wimbledon Championship began on 9 July 1877, on a lawn behind a croquet club.

title: Crossfire Hurricane
why: The Rolling Stones played their first gig at the Marquee on 12 July 1962.

title: Kingdom of Heaven
why: The First Crusade took Jerusalem on 15 July 1099; Ridley Scott's film is the century of consequences.
alt: St Swithin's Day; the Turkish coup attempt, 15 July 2016

title: The Romanovs: An Imperial Family
why: The Ipatiev House cellar, Ekaterinburg, in the early hours of 17 July 1918.

title: Chappaquiddick
why: Mary Jo Kopechne's body is recovered from the Oldsmobile on the morning of 19 July 1969 — ten hours after Kennedy walked away from the bridge.

title: Apollo 11
why: Armstrong steps onto the Moon at 02:56 UTC on 21 July 1969 — which is why Britain watched it in the middle of the night.
alt: First Man (2018); the Scopes trial verdict, 21 July 1925 — Inherit the Wind

title: Secret of the Incas
why: Hiram Bingham reached Machu Picchu on 24 July 1911; Charlton Heston in a leather jacket and fedora did the rest.

title: Crip Camp
why: The Americans with Disabilities Act is signed on 26 July 1990 — the destination of a story that starts at a scruffy summer camp in the Catskills.

title: Oh! What a Lovely War
why: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia on 28 July 1914 and the pier at Brighton fills up.

title: Elizabeth: The Golden Age
why: The Armada is broken at Gravelines on 29 July 1588, and the wind does the rest.
alt: The wedding of Charles and Diana, 29 July 1981

title: The Fog of War
why: McNamara, on camera, on the Gulf of Tonkin incident of 2 August 1964 — the thing that may not have happened, and the war it started.

title: Frost/Nixon
why: Opens with the helicopter on the South Lawn: Nixon leaves the White House on the morning of 9 August 1974.
alt: Nagasaki, 9 August 1945; Charlie Says — the Cielo Drive murders, night of 8/9 August 1969

title: Dolores Claiborne
why: Everything hinges on a total solar eclipse — and Britain got its own on 11 August 1999, the last until 2090.

title: Earth
why: Partition takes effect on 14/15 August 1947 and a Lahore childhood is cut in half.
alt: Viceroy's House (2017); VJ Day announced, 14 August 1945

title: Blow-Up
why: World Photography Day: the daguerreotype was given to the world on 19 August 1839. Antonioni's photographer keeps enlarging until there's nothing there.

title: Mona Lisa
why: Vincenzo Peruggia walked out of the Louvre with the Mona Lisa under his smock on 21 August 1911, and made her the most famous painting on earth.

title: Mother Teresa
why: Born Anjeze Gonxhe Bojaxhiu in Skopje on 26 August 1910.
alt: Women's Equality Day — the 19th Amendment certified, 26 August 1920; Crecy, 26 August 1346

title: Dr. Strangelove
why: The Moscow–Washington hotline went live on 30 August 1963. Kubrick had already worked out how the call would go.

title: Westerplatte
why: The Schleswig-Holstein opens fire on the Polish depot at 04:45 on 1 September 1939 — the first shots of the war, and 182 men hold for a week.
alt: Katyn; the Titanic wreck found, 1 September 1985

title: Plymouth Adventure
why: The Mayflower finally clears Plymouth on 6 September 1620 with 102 passengers and a leaking beam.

title: A Walk in the Sun
why: A platoon comes ashore at Salerno at dawn on 9 September 1943 and spends the whole film walking six miles inland.

title: Particle Fever
why: The Large Hadron Collider is switched on for the first time on 10 September 2008; the physicists watch a screen and hold their breath.

title: Isadora
why: Isadora Duncan's scarf catches in the wheel of a Bugatti in Nice on 14 September 1927 — the film's opening and closing image.

title: Viva Zapata!
why: Mexican Independence Day — the Grito de Dolores, 16 September 1810.

title: Iceman
why: Two hikers found Otzi melting out of the Similaun glacier on 19 September 1991; this film imagines his last week, 5,300 years earlier, in a language nobody speaks.

title: The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey
why: The Hobbit was published on 21 September 1937. Also the International Day of Peace, which Bilbo would have approved of.

title: Ad Astra
why: Neptune was found on 23 September 1846, exactly where the mathematics said it would be. Roy McBride goes there to find his father.

title: 1991: The Year Punk Broke
why: Nevermind was released on 24 September 1991, in the middle of the tour this film is shot on.

title: The Ernest Green Story
why: The 101st Airborne walks the Little Rock Nine through the doors of Central High on 25 September 1957.

title: The Man Who Saved the World
why: Just after midnight on 26 September 1983 Stanislav Petrov's screen says five American missiles are inbound, and he decides it is a fault.

title: Thrilla in Manila
why: Ali and Frazier, fourteen rounds in 40-degree heat, 1 October 1975 — 'the closest thing to dying that I know of'.

title: 12 Strong
why: The air campaign in Afghanistan opens on 7 October 2001 and twelve men go in on horseback behind it.
alt: Poe dies in Baltimore, 7 October 1849; Lepanto, 7 October 1571

title: Vajont
why: At 22:39 on 9 October 1963 the mountain slid into the reservoir; the wave that cleared the dam erased Longarone within minutes, in the first hour of the 10th.

title: Saturday Night
why: The ninety minutes before 11:30pm on 11 October 1975, in real time, as Saturday Night Live goes on air for the first time.
alt: Zodiac — Paul Stine killed in Presidio Heights, 11 October 1969

title: Nuit Noire, 17 octobre 1961
why: The title is the date: the Paris police attack an Algerian demonstration and throw men into the Seine, 17 October 1961.
alt: Cache (2005), which is haunted by the same night

title: The Boat That Rocked
why: The BBC was founded on 18 October 1922 — and this is the film about everyone who wanted to broadcast around it.

title: Back to Bataan
why: MacArthur wades ashore at Leyte on 20 October 1944: 'I have returned.'
alt: The Sydney Opera House opens, 20 October 1973

title: Longitude
why: Four ships pile onto the Scillies on 22 October 1707 for want of a way to find longitude — which is what sets John Harrison building clocks.
alt: Kennedy's missile broadcast, 22 October 1962 — Thirteen Days

title: The Interpreter
why: United Nations Day: the Charter came into force on 24 October 1945. The only feature ever allowed to film inside the General Assembly.

title: The Taking of Pelham One Two Three
why: The New York subway opened on 27 October 1904. Seventy years later, four men in hats hijacked a car of it.
alt: Black Saturday of the Cuban Missile Crisis, 27 October 1962
